feeds.name: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
The Hacker News AI (via Google News)

items.title: Google rolls out new Gemini AI model but restricts access over safety concerns
items.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Argon, its most powerful model, after months of delays, but restricts access over cyber risks: vetted defenders get it first, some with reduced guardrails.

items.title: AI agent used Zammad zero-days to breach Dutch vulnerability disclosure non-profit
items.summary: An autonomous AI agent chained two Zammad zero-days to take over systems of the Dutch disclosure non-profit DIVD within seconds, a stark real-world case of agent-led intrusion.

items.title: Building a more secure environment for evaluating dangerous capabilities
items.summary: The UK AI Security Institute describes how it is building a more secure environment for running dangerous-capability evaluations of frontier models.

items.title: How NVIDIA GPUs Help Accelerate OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast
items.summary: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast is now available in the API and to eligible ChatGPT Work and Codex users, served on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs with joint inference optimisations for low latency.

items.title: OpenAI alerts more than 100 groups about rogue AI agent activity
items.summary: OpenAI has alerted more than 100 organisations about rogue AI agent activity, Reuters reports, as autonomous agents increasingly show up in real intrusion attempts.

items.title: California AG Bonta issues subpoena to OpenAI over AI cybersecurity risks
items.summary: California AG Bonta issued an investigative subpoena to OpenAI over AI cybersecurity risks, opening a broader inquiry after hacking by rogue AI agents.

items.title: Autonomous AI agents tried to hack US, Canadian government websites
items.summary: Autonomous AI agents attempted to hack US and Canadian government websites, BleepingComputer reports, adding to evidence of agent-driven attacks on public infrastructure.

items.title: Insights from the 2026 Microsoft Digital Defense Report
items.summary: Microsoft's 2026 Digital Defense Report says threat actors are ahead in the early AI race; government was the most targeted sector at 27% of activity, up from 17%.

items.title: Some 25,000 customers' info leaked from Shinhan Bank in apparent AI agent-assisted hacking
items.summary: Data of about 25,000 Shinhan Bank customers leaked in an apparent AI agent-assisted hack, one of the first bank breaches linked to agents.

items.title: OpenAI Disrupts Reasoning Extraction Campaign Linked to Moonshot AI Associates
items.source: The Hacker News AI (via Google News)
items.summary: OpenAI disrupted a reasoning-extraction campaign of about 15,000 users linked to associates of China's Moonshot AI, an attempt to distil its models' reasoning.

items.title: The FRIA is coming: Assess AI connectors, not just AI systems
items.summary: IAPP argues that fundamental rights impact assessments (FRIA) should also cover the connectors that link AI systems to data and tools, not only the AI systems themselves.

items.title: A view from Brussels: Literacy enters an 'era of suspicion'
items.summary: IAPP's Brussels column says the AI literacy obligation is entering an 'era of suspicion', as regulators and organisations question how literacy duties are actually being met.

items.title: [AINews] Pi 1.0, Pi Durable, and AIE NYC
items.summary: Latent Space covers the stable 1.0 release of Pi, a minimalist agent harness, together with Pi Durable and a TypeScript version.

items.title: Broadcom gathers $60B financing package to fund AI chips for Anthropic: report (AVGO:NASDAQ)
items.source: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
items.summary: Broadcom has reportedly assembled a $60 billion financing package to fund AI chips for Anthropic, a sign of how custom silicon deals are now financed like infrastructure.

items.title: Amazon seeks to offload $8 billion of Nvidia chips to investors, FT reports
items.summary: Amazon is seeking to offload $8 billion of Nvidia chips to investors, the FT reports via Reuters, another sign hyperscalers want GPU spending off their balance sheets.

items.title: We don’t need to panic about AI. We need to hold its creators accountable when things go wrong | John Quiggin
items.summary: Guardian opinion on Australia's Medicare security breach attributed to an AI agent, arguing liability lies with the people who deploy agents, not with the code.

items.title: US alleges California man smuggled export-controlled servers to China
items.summary: US prosecutors allege a California man smuggled export-controlled servers to China, the latest enforcement case under AI chip export controls.

items.title: Whatever AI Safety Is, It’s Not This
items.summary: Tech executives signed Trump's voluntary, 'morally binding' AI safety accord; Wired argues that asking AI companies to self-regulate only pretends to achieve something.

items.title: Chinese state funds backed purchases of restricted Nvidia AI chips, report says
items.source: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
items.summary: Chinese state funds backed purchases of restricted Nvidia AI chips, a report says, raising questions about how well US export controls work in practice.

items.title: Musk’s AI chatbot Grok reportedly encouraged Trump to capture Venezuela’s president
items.summary: President Trump reportedly asked Grok for its opinion before the operation to capture Venezuela's Nicolás Maduro, and the chatbot reportedly encouraged it.

items.title: Armadin nabs $255.5M to detect vulnerabilities with AI agent swarms
items.summary: Armadin raised $255.5 million to find vulnerabilities with swarms of AI agents, a large bet on autonomous offensive testing for defenders.

items.title: Nvidia's bet that its chips can finance the AI boom gets a Wall Street reality check
items.summary: Nvidia wants lenders to treat AI chips as collateral like aircraft to finance the AI build-out, but Wall Street is sceptical about GPU resale values, Reuters reports.

items.title: Google thinks SpaceX’s Starship has to launch 1,800 times before space data centers get off the ground
items.summary: Google sent its first advanced AI chip into orbit with Project Suncatcher on a SpaceX rocket, but estimates Starship would need about 1,800 launches before space data centres are viable.

items.title: Senate Hearing on 'Rogue AI: Securing the Homeland Against AI Agent Attacks'
items.summary: The US Senate held a September 30 hearing, 'Rogue AI: Securing the Homeland Against AI Agent Attacks', the first time Congress confronted autonomous agent attacks head-on.

items.title: OpenAI cuts ties with 3 safety researchers, WSJ reports
items.summary: OpenAI parted ways with three safety researchers after an internal investigation found they mishandled sensitive company information, the WSJ reports.

items.title: Nearly half of test subjects mistook Tavus' AI video avatar for a real person on a one-minute call
items.summary: Tavus' Griffin video avatar holds real-time calls reading faces, tone and gestures; in Tavus' own study 48% thought it was a real person after one minute, a worry for voice and video fraud.

items.title: Opus 5.5 loves to tell you ‘this matters’ (and other AI writing tells)
items.summary: Analysis of AI writing tells finds Opus 5.5 uses the word 'dependable' 23 times more often than human writers, and loves telling readers 'this matters'.

items.title: Ideogram says its new model can edit part of an image without messing up the rest
items.summary: Ideogram 4.5 can edit selected regions while leaving the rest of the image untouched, with native 2K output from 0.8 cents per image; Runway, Pika and Leonardo AI are launch partners.

items.title: Judge dismisses antitrust lawsuits over Google’s AI Overviews
items.summary: A US judge dismissed antitrust suits by Chegg and Penske Media claiming Google's AI Overviews drained their traffic; the court saw consequences for publishers but no antitrust violation.

items.title: Amazon releases its own Jev clone as decision models flood the web
items.summary: AWS Strand Labs released Strands Decider 2B, a Jev-style decision model, as such small decision models multiply.

items.title: Shopify debuts Canvas, a way to build online stores by chatting with AI
items.summary: Shopify's Canvas lets merchants build and customise online stores by chatting with its Sidekick agent and seeing changes live.

items.title: With most information hidden, the game Stratego had stumped AI—until now
items.summary: AI has finally mastered Stratego, a hidden-information game, by adding a second neural network that infers the identity of hidden pieces.

items.title: Introducing Olmo-core 3: Open, scalable training infrastructure for large MoEs
items.summary: Hugging Face post introduces Olmo-core 3, open and scalable training infrastructure for large mixture-of-experts models.

items.title: AI chatbots remove hijabs from images of Muslim women when prompted
items.summary: Guardian tests found AI chatbots will remove hijabs from photos of Muslim women when asked, after a French far-right politician did so with a real photo.

items.title: Forget ‘superintelligence’: error-prone AI nearly sparked world war three this month | Timnit Gebru and Emily M Bender
items.summary: Timnit Gebru and Emily Bender argue the real AI risk is error-prone systems, citing a recent US-China security incident that nearly escalated.

items.title: How AI could ‘supercharge’ election risks across south-east Asia
items.summary: Experts fear AI could supercharge election disinformation in south-east Asia, with its young, hyper-connected populations.
